title: Synthesis and Characterization of CMK Porous Carbons Modified with Metals Applied to Hydrogen Uptake and Storage
material_description: CMK-1 | ordered mesoporous carbon replica of MCM-48 silica: sucrose with H2SO4 by two-step incipient-wetness impregnation, carbonized at 1173 K for 4 h under N2, silica removed with HF
purification_method: silica template dissolved with 5 wt% HF at room temperature (twice); carbon filtered, washed with deionized water and ethanol, dried
source_location: main-13.png (p. 63), Table 3, row CMK-1, column H2 sorption (wt%)** (footnote: at 10 bar and 77 K); same sample, temperature and pressure as the 10 bar end of the Figure 25 CMK-1 curve (main-29.png, p. 79)
notes: Table 3 footnote: 'H2 sorption at 10 bar and 77 K'. Same measurement as the 10 bar end of the Figure 25 CMK-1 isotherm (black Ads. line, open-square Des. markers), but that curve lies under the CMK-3 (green) and Ni-CMK-1 (red) series and could not be digitized, so no digitized point is given and isotherm_point_count is left empty (Des. markers hidden). In Figure 25 the CMK-1 open squares are covered by CMK-3 markers that end at 2.18 wt% (digitized), above the printed 2.1. Characterization from Table 3 (p. 63): 'Area (m2/g)' printed without a method (BET is not named for Table 3), from N2 adsorption-desorption at 77 K (ASAP 2020, samples purged at 673 K, Section 2.8); 'VP (cm3 g-1) mesoporous volume' stored as mesopore_volume_cm3_g (method not stated); BJH pore diameter. BET range not stated. H2 method (p. 56): 'ASAP 2050 apparatus properly calibrated', 77 K, 0-10 bar, H2 99.9999%; no manufacturer and no free-volume or calibration method stated; coded volumetric_sieverts because the ASAP 2050 is a volumetric (manometric) analyzer, so basis_inferred = excess by the instrumental default; the paper does not name the uptake basis. Degassing printed: 523 K for 8 h under vacuum (stored 249.85 C). No sample mass, uncertainty or replicate stated.

purification_method: silica template dissolved with 5 wt% HF at room temperature (twice); carbon filtered, washed with deionized water and ethanol, dried
source_location: main-29.png (p. 79), Figure 25, Ni-CMK-1 Des. (red filled squares), marker at 8.99 bar
notes: Figure 25 Des. marker (legend 'Des.'), digitized as the marker centroid (digitize_figure.py --mode markers); archive: fig25_NiCMK1_des.json. isotherm_point_count = 41 Des. markers counted (0.25-bar spacing from 0.25 to 10 bar, plus one at 0 bar); the Ads. branch is a line without markers. Characterization from Table 3 (p. 63): 'Area (m2/g)' printed without a method (BET is not named for Table 3), from N2 adsorption-desorption at 77 K (ASAP 2020, samples purged at 673 K, Section 2.8); 'VP (cm3 g-1) mesoporous volume' stored as mesopore_volume_cm3_g (method not stated); BJH pore diameter. BET range not stated. Metal loading: ICP 5.5 wt% Ni in the reduced sample (p. 54, cited to ref. [13]); EDS 5.3 wt% Ni; XPS Ni 0.625 at%. H2 method (p. 56): 'ASAP 2050 apparatus properly calibrated', 77 K, 0-10 bar, H2 99.9999%; no manufacturer and no free-volume or calibration method stated; coded volumetric_sieverts because the ASAP 2050 is a volumetric (manometric) analyzer, so basis_inferred = excess by the instrumental default; the paper does not name the uptake basis. Degassing printed: 523 K for 8 h under vacuum (stored 249.85 C). No sample mass, uncertainty or replicate stated.
